question.prompt:
Raashan, Sylvia, and Ted play the following game. Each starts with \( \$1.\) A bell rings every \(15\) seconds, at which time each of the players who currently has money simultaneously chooses one of the other two players independently and at random and gives \(\$1\) to that player. What is the probability that after the bell has rung \(2019\) times, each player will have \(\$1?\)

(For example, Raashan and Ted may each decide to give \(\$1\) to Sylvia, and Sylvia may decide to give her dollar to Ted, at which point Raashan will have \(\$0,\) Sylvia will have \(\$2,\) and Ted will have \(\$1,\) and that is the end of the first round of play. In the second round Raashan has no money to give, but Sylvia and Ted might choose each other to give their \( \$1\) to, and the holdings will be the same at the end of the second round.)

solutions.title: Compare the two holding types
solutions.explanation:
The key observation is that only two types of holdings can occur, and both give the same chance of returning to one dollar each.

The total money always remains \(\$3\). A player who starts a round with money sends a dollar to someone else, and that recipient still has at least that incoming dollar after the simultaneous exchange. Thus the sender cannot finish with all \(\$3\). A player who starts with no money can receive at most two dollars. Consequently, nobody can finish with \(\$3\), so the only possible holding types are \((1,1,1)\) and a rearrangement of \((2,1,0)\).

Consider each starting type:

1. From \((1,1,1)\), suppose Raashan chooses Sylvia. To finish with one dollar each, Ted must give to Raashan, and Sylvia must give to Ted. These two independent choices have probability
\[
\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac14.
\]
If Raashan instead chooses Ted, the same reasoning gives probability \(\tfrac14\).

2. From \((2,1,0)\), name the players so that Raashan has two dollars, Sylvia has one, and Ted has none. After sending their dollars, Raashan retains one and Sylvia retains none. To finish with one each, Raashan must send to Sylvia, and Sylvia must send to Ted. Again the probability is \(\tfrac14\). Relabeling the players covers every rearrangement of this type.

Let \(p_n\) be the probability of one dollar each after \(n\) rings, with \(p_0=1\). Splitting according to the preceding holding type gives, for every \(n\ge1\),
\[
p_n=\frac14p_{n-1}+\frac14(1-p_{n-1})=\frac14.
\]
Therefore \(p_{2019}=\boxed{\tfrac14}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
